result.topic_en: Gauss sets out a method for computing the orbit of a celestial body from four observed longitudes and two latitudes, defining the notation and the system of equations to be solved for z' and z''.
result.transcription:
99 [-133-]
[1807 Jan. Tagebuch 129]
Methode aus vier Längen und zwei Breiten
die Bahn eines Himmelskörpers zu berechnen.

Die Zeichen
Beobachtete Längen $\alpha, \alpha', \alpha'', \alpha'''$
Beobachtete Breiten $\beta', \beta''$.
Längen der Erde $l, l', l'', l'''$
Abstände der Erde v. d. S. $R, R', R'', R'''$
Abst. d. H. v. S. $r, r', r'', r'''$
(01), (12), (23) die [-Dreiecke-] {+Räume+} an der Sonne div. durch die Zeiten.
Die Zeiten $t, t', t'', t'''$
Die Längen in der Bahn $w, w', w'', w'''$

Abst. v. der Erde in der 2 3 Beob. $\rho'$ $\rho''$
$\delta' + $ [?]

$V' = \frac{r'r'}{rr''(01)(12)\cos\frac{1}{2}(w'-w)\cos\frac{1}{2}(w''-w)\cos\frac{1}{2}(w''-w')}$
$V'' = \frac{r''r''}{r'r'''(12)(23)\cos\frac{1}{2}(w''-w')\cos\frac{1}{2}(w'''-w')\cos\frac{1}{2}(w'''-w'')}$

$\frac{t'-t}{t''-t'}\frac{(12)}{(01)} = \frac{1}{P'}$
$\frac{t'''-t''}{t''-t'}\frac{(12)}{(23)} = \frac{1}{P''}$

[-Die Gleich-]
Man mache
$\mathrm{tg}\,\gamma' = \frac{\tan\beta'}{\sin(\alpha'-l')}$ ; $\sin\delta' = \frac{\sin\beta'}{\sin\gamma'}$, $\cos\delta' = \cos\beta'\cos(\alpha'-l')$
$\mathrm{tg}\,\gamma'' = \frac{\tan\beta''}{\sin(\alpha''-l'')}$ ; $\sin\delta'' = \frac{\sin\beta''}{\sin\gamma''}$, $\cos\delta'' = \cos\beta''\cos(\alpha''-l'')$

Hiernächst wird $z'$ und $z''$ durch die Combination folgender Gleichungen best.

$z'' = -e' + \frac{d'(z'+c')}{1+\frac{b'}{(z'z'+a'a')^{3:2}}}$
$z' = -e'' + \frac{d''(z''+c'')}{1+\frac{b''}{(z''z''+a''a'')^{3:2}}}$

$\Delta' + R'\cos\delta' = z'$
$\Delta'' + R''\cos\delta'' = z''$
$R'\sin\delta' = a'$
$R''\sin\delta'' = a''$
$r'r' = z'z' + a'a'$
$r''r'' = z''z'' + a''a''$
$\frac{1}{2}V'(t'-t)(t''-t')M^2 = b'$
$\frac{1}{2}V''(t''-t')(t'''-t')M^2 = b''$

$c' = -R'\cos\delta' + \frac{R'\sin(l'-\alpha)}{\cos\beta'\sin(\alpha'-\alpha)}$
$c'' = -R''\cos\delta'' + \frac{R''\sin(\alpha'''-l'')}{\cos\beta''\sin(\alpha'''-\alpha'')}$
$d' = \frac{t''-t}{t'-t}\frac{(01)}{(02)}\frac{\sin\alpha'-\alpha}{\sin(\alpha''-\alpha)}\frac{\cos\beta'}{\cos\beta''}(1+P')$
$d'' = \frac{t'''-t'}{t'''-t''}\frac{[-(23)-]}{(13)}\frac{\sin\alpha'''-\alpha''}{\sin\alpha'''-\alpha'}\frac{\cos\beta''}{\cos\beta'}(1+P'')$
$e' = -R''\cos\delta'' + \frac{R''\sin(l''-\alpha)}{\cos\beta''\sin(\alpha''-\alpha)} + [-\frac{(01)}{(12)}\frac{t'-t'}{t'-t}-] \frac{R\sin(l-\alpha)P'}{\cos\beta''[-P-]\sin(\alpha''-\alpha)}$
$e'' = -R'\cos\delta' + \frac{R'\sin(\alpha'''-l')}{\cos\beta'\sin(\alpha'''-\alpha')} + [-\frac{(23)}{(12)}\frac{t''-t'}{t'''-t''}-] \frac{R'''\sin(\alpha'''-l''')P''}{[-P''-]\cos\beta'\sin(\alpha'''-\alpha')}$

methods.what: Orbit determination of a celestial body from four longitudes and two latitudes
methods.quote: Methode aus vier Längen und zwei Breiten\ndie Bahn eines Himmelskörpers zu berechnen.

methods.what: Definition of V' via radii, sector-triangle ratios and half-angle cosines of orbital longitude differences
Definition of P', P'' from time intervals and sector ratios
Auxiliary angles gamma, delta from observed latitude and elongation
Coupled nonlinear equations for z', z'' to be solved iteratively
Relations between z, a, distances and heliocentric radius
Coefficient b' from V', time intervals and constant M
Coefficients c', d', e' in terms of observations
